cards.text: Jesus has just been taken up into heaven while His apostles watched (Acts 1:9). Now they head back to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives, a Sabbath day's journey away. So it's close, friend. That's 'forget the car, we're WALKING' close.

cards.question: Back in Jerusalem, where do the apostles go?

answers.text: An upper room where they're staying
The house of Simon the tanner

cards.text: Here's who's in that room: Peter and John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James. Two Jameses in one room, so somebody get these men some NAME TAGS.

cards.question: In the upper room are Peter and John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James. How many apostles is that?
With one accord, the apostles in the upper room all continue in ___.

cards.text: And it's not just the eleven in there. The women are praying right alongside them, and they're not the only ones.

cards.question: Besides the women, who else is praying with the apostles?

answers.text: Mary the mother of Jesus and His brothers
Lazarus and his sisters Mary and Martha

cards.text: In those days, Peter stands up among the brothers to say something. And I don't know about you, but when the guy who talks the most stands up, I'm pulling up a CHAIR.

cards.question: The gathering Peter speaks to is about five hundred people.

cards.text: Peter says the Scripture had to be fulfilled. It's about Judas, who became a guide for those who arrested Jesus.

cards.question: Peter says the Holy Spirit foretold this about Judas through the mouth of ___.
Peter says Judas was one of their number and shared in their ministry.

cards.text: Then the story pauses Peter's speech for a moment. With the reward for his wickedness, Judas bought a field, and there he fell headlong and burst open.

cards.question: Everyone in Jerusalem hears about what happened to Judas. In their own language, what do they call his field?

cards.text: Back to Peter. He quotes the book of Psalms, "May his place be deserted; let there be no one to dwell in it," and then he adds one more line.

cards.question: The second line Peter quotes from Psalms asks for someone else to take Judas's position.

cards.text: So Peter says they need to choose one of the men who were with them while the Lord Jesus went in and out among them. Not somebody who wandered in last week for the free COOKIES.

cards.question: How far back does Peter say the new man has to have been with them?

answers.text: From John's baptism until Jesus was taken up
From the wedding at Cana until the cross
From the Sermon on the Mount until the tomb

cards.question: Peter says the new man must become a witness with them of Jesus's ___.

cards.text: So they put forward two men: Joseph called Barsabbas, also known as Justus, and Matthias. Three names on one man, so forget a name tag, Joseph needs a BANNER.

cards.question: Two good men, one spot. What do they do before anything is decided?

answers.text: They let the two men speak

cards.question: In their prayer, they tell the Lord that He knows everyone's ___.

cards.text: They ask the Lord to show them which of the two He has chosen for the ministry and apostleship that Judas abandoned. They want HIS pick, not theirs.

cards.question: To decide between Joseph and Matthias, they take a vote.
They cast lots. Who does the lot fall to?

cards.text: So Matthias is added to the eleven apostles. Friend, I spent years counting dust in the back of a junk drawer, and even I can tell you that makes TWELVE.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: 'Jesus has just been taken up...', 'Now they head back...', 'So it's close, friend.' and 'That's 'forget the car, we're WALKING' close.' The limit is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: Nothing before this true or false card hints at how big the gathering is, so the pick is pure luck. The answer is False, and no card ever says the real number (about a hundred and twenty, Acts 1:15). The baker leaves Prep without that detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Most of the choice cards in stop 1 can't be reasoned out from earlier cards. Card 2 (the upper room), card 7 (Mary and His brothers), card 9 (the size of the gathering), card 11 (David) and card 14 (Akeldama) are all discovery questions. That is 5 of the stop's 9 choice cards, so informed guesses are not the majority.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The question calls Joseph and Matthias 'Two good men.' Acts 1:23 only says 'two men.' The text never calls them good.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The story card's line 'They want HIS pick, not theirs' rules out a vote. That gives away the answer to card 8, which asks whether they take a vote.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Matthias is the odd one out. It is one short name, while both wrong answers are longer look-alike phrases starting 'Joseph called Bar...'. The right answer stands out from the other two.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
